extracted.subtask_description: A journalistic news article reporting that Newsweek retracted a story about alleged Quran desecration, summarizing the retraction, source issues, official responses, and consequences. The page exemplifies standards and failings in reporting that led to international unrest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify and corroborate serious allegations before publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports of wrongdoing should be corroborated with independent evidence; after a review of more than 25,000 documents investigators 'found only one incident recorded in the prison logs involving a Quran' and 'we can't find anything to substantiate the allegations that appeared in Newsweek.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do comprehensive document and record checks and seek independent corroboration before publishing explosive claims. Anti-pattern: publishing allegations based on incomplete record reviews or without documentary corroboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid relying on a single source for explosive claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The original Newsweek article 'said only a single source was used' and that source later 'backed away from his initial story.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not publish sensational or high-impact claims that rest on a single source's account; seek multiple independent sources. If a claim is source-limited, label it clearly and treat it with skepticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek and document official comment prior to publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Newsweek said it went to the 'extraordinary length' of showing the story to a Pentagon official for a response before publication; that official challenged other aspects but not the Quran detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact relevant officials for response and record challenges or confirmations from them. Document which officials were asked and what responses were received. Anti-pattern: proceeding without attempting to obtain comment from implicated parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be transparent about sources and any subsequent changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Whitaker said the source was 'known to be credible and in a position to know the things he was telling us,' yet that source later said he wasn't sure what he'd read; Newsweek later said its senior government source had 'backed away' from his initial story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose key sourcing constraints and be explicit when sources change or contradict earlier claims. When a source recants or is uncertain, clearly explain that to readers and correct the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue prompt, clear retractions or corrections when errors are found
rubrics_metrics.description: Newsweek 'retracted our original story' and Whitaker wrote that 'we regret' that any part of the story was wrong; the magazine later issued a fuller statement disavowing the detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting is shown to be incorrect, publish an unequivocal retraction or correction promptly and prominently. Guidance includes acknowledging specific errors and explaining how they occurred. Anti-pattern: delayed, partial, or buried corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider and weigh potential harm and international consequences of reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The report 'was blamed for anti-American riots' in Afghanistan and elsewhere; officials said 'People are dead' and warned that journalists 'need to be very careful about what they say.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess possible real-world consequences of reporting, especially in volatile contexts; weigh public interest against foreseeable harms. If reporting could inflame tensions, take extra care in verification, framing, and outreach to affected communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take responsibility to mitigate fallout after harmful errors
rubrics_metrics.description: White House officials said the magazine 'will have to do more to repair the damage done' and urged Newsweek to 'spread the word to the Muslim world' about the retraction; diplomats worked to 'spread the word' about the correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After harmful mistakes, proactively communicate corrections to affected audiences and stakeholders, using appropriate channels and sustained effort to mitigate damage. Single retractions may be insufficient; plan outreach where the impact was significant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain editorial accountability and robust internal review processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Whitaker said everyone at Newsweek 'behaved professionally' and the magazine went to 'extraordinary length' to seek comment, yet the error occurred; officials criticized the approach as 'allow[ing] them to run this story without proper examination beforehand.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have clear editorial checks for high-risk stories (multiple editors, source vetting, document verification). After errors, review internal processes to identify breakdowns. Anti-pattern: assuming procedural compliance guarantees accuracy without critical review.
